data.description: Last week, hackers drained $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, in what blockchain analysts call the largest theft of any kind in history. The FBI blames TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit, though North Korea denies it. Patrick Boyle looks at how the Binance hack worked: a fake job interview, Binance’s own internal AI tool, an Ethereum feature called EIP-7702, and fifty pre-signed transactions. It covers why Tether and Circle could freeze billions in stolen stablecoins while the hackers’ bitcoin and ether stayed out of reach, how North Korea launders and cashes out stolen crypto, and why bitcoin barely moved while Coinbase and Circle shares fell. We tell the story of how Freud’s nephew turned bacon into a doctor-approved breakfast, and how the TSA spent nearly $1 billion training officers to spot liars, with nothing to show for it. We walk through the one test that shows when persuasion crosses into manipulation, and the tactics advertisers, propagandists, and con artists have been running on you for a century. data.description: In this episode, RealLifeLore examines why tourism to Afghanistan has risen since the Taliban returned to power in 2021. Despite severe travel warnings from Western governments, thousands of foreign visitors are traveling to the country for its landscapes, history, and relative security compared with the war years. The episode looks at how the Taliban uses tourism for revenue and international legitimacy, the risks tourists still face, restrictions on women and local freedoms, and how countries such as Russia are increasingly engaging with the Taliban government. data.description: Are you looking to break free from the trap of a 9 to 5 job in the modern economy? Today, he is fully dedicated to disrupting the American healthcare industry through his revolutionary online pharmacy, Cost Plus Drugs.In this episode, he explains:■ The AI Illusion: How artificial intelligence is simply a brute force pattern matcher that lacks true human intelligence, meaning the real edge belongs to humans who leverage it to “out prepare” and “out learn” the competition.■ The Power of Sales: Why very successful business is fundamentally built on sales, and mastering the ability to handle objections and rejection guarantees you a job for life.■ The Danger of Quick Money: How modern social media algorithms feed youth an illusion of instant wealth, holding back a generation that refuses to put in the grueling preparation required to master a skill.■ The Chemistry of Leadership: How turning around a failing sports franchise or a business requires ruthless commitment to team culture, hiring slowly, firing fast, and replacing ego with collective alignment.■ The True Definition of Success: Why true wealth is ultimately about controlling your own time and destiny rather than buying luxury items, and prioritizing family above all else remains the ultimate life achievement.(00:00:00) Intro(00:02:16) Why Being Adaptable Matters(00:03:09) My Upbringing(00:04:40) My First Business: Selling Garbage Bags at 12(00:06:18) How to Become a Great Salesperson(00:08:34) The Biggest Mistakes Young Entrepreneurs Make(00:11:17) What All Millionaires Have in Common(00:13:38) How I Transformed the Dallas Mavericks(00:18:48) Hate Your Job but Have Little Savings?
